findings.what: Two register rows born from ONE invoice each name the other as `relation: "successor"`. 0041 SS9.4's designed shape is one register row per cost line ("a multi-unit leg births one row and freight on a second line births a second row BY DESIGN", 0041:2591-2593), so a two-cost-line invoice is ordinary, not exotic. Both rows share `acquisition_entry_id`, therefore the same document, therefore the `source_document` arm hits; and because they also share `approved_at`, `case when ge.approved_at >= e.approved_at then 'successor' else 'predecessor' end` resolves to `successor` in BOTH directions. The History tab renders that word in its "Relation" column (`r.relation === "predecessor" ? t("history.predecessor") : t("history.successor")`), so a professional is told a co-acquired sibling superseded the asset — a mutually contradictory accounting claim on the very tab AC4 adds to show corrections. The "Derived from: Same source document" column and `history.derivationNote` soften it but do not withdraw the word.
findings.evidence: On the from-scratch rig (55604/clara_639r) I approved one document-lane entry with two debits on the enrolled cost account 200-D41 (RM5000 compressor + RM400 freight) + one bank credit: `node --test <scratch>/adv639b.test.mjs` -> `assets born from ONE two-cost-line invoice: 2`. Then `select f.id, f.cost_cents, clara._fa_acquisition_history(f.id)->'related' from clara.fixed_assets f where f.acquisition_entry_id='2140547c-3da1-4ee4-b27b-8b9e810763d2'` returned, for dd96ccf8 (RM5000): `[{"link":"source_document","asset_id":"bf169e33...","relation":"successor","cost_cents":40000,...}]` and for bf169e33 (RM400): `[{"link":"source_document","asset_id":"dd96ccf8...","relation":"successor","cost_cents":500000,...}]`. Each claims the other as its successor. No battery cell covers a multi-line acquisition — `p639.correction.chain` uses two separate single-line entries.
findings.fix: In the `source_document` lateral arm (0201:463), exclude the row's own acquisition entry: `(v_doc is not null and ge.doc = v_doc and ge.id <> e.id)`; co-acquired siblings then either drop out or, better, get their own vocabulary (`link: 'co_acquired_on_same_document'`, no predecessor/successor word) with a matching `history.links.*` string in en.json and a neutral Relation cell. Separately make the ordering strict — `ge.approved_at > e.approved_at` -> `successor`, `<` -> `predecessor` — so equal timestamps can never resolve to `successor` on both sides. Add a behavioural cell for the two-cost-line invoice beside `p639.correction.chain`.

findings.what: brief-639.md:19 named the two things a reviewer demanded on the sibling ticket and told this worker to "Write those in, not after": **a raced concurrency cell** and **a merge-order table**. Neither shipped. The battery has no two-session cell at all (`Promise.all`/barrier/advisory-lock race: zero hits across the file), even though the ticket's own core takes `pg_advisory_xact_lock(203005004, hashtext(client))` then `clara.fixed_assets ... for update` (0201:698-701) and the whole point of `complete-once` is what happens when two callers arrive together. The final report likewise carries no merge-order table, although 0201's prestate pins two `prosrc` sha256 values and its tail T.5 pins an exact SIX-name `_subledger_on_approve` caller array — both of which 0199 (#650) and 0200 (#647) land in front of, and either would make 0201 refuse to apply rather than merge cleanly.
findings.evidence: `grep -nE 'race|concurren|barrier|Promise\.all' packages/db/tests/fixed-asset-acquisition.test.mjs` -> only three unrelated hits (lines 530/534/541, a sequential second-client fixture). `grep -c '^test(' ...` -> 18; none of the 18 names is a race. The report's "Commands and counts" and "Assumptions" sections contain no merge-order table. I supplied the missing race myself: two `clara_runtime` sessions in explicit transactions, session 2 entering while session 1 held the advisory lock, barrier released by session 1's COMMIT -> `race -> s1 ok=true err=null | s2 ok=false err=CLR37/fa_particulars_already_complete`, and `clara.fixed_assets.useful_life_months = 60` (exactly one effect). I also measured op-key replay (same key + same payload returns the identical receipt, journal count unmoved) and payload conflict (CLR10 `op_key reused with different args`). So the behaviour is right — the evidence is missing.

Add a merge-order table to 639-final.md listing 0199 and 0200 against the three things 0201 pins (the two `prosrc` shas and the six-name caller array) and stating that neither predecessor touches them (DECISIONS §1.3).

findings.what: The comment at :757 states "NO ORACLE: an unknown client and another firm's client answer the same way." Measured, they do not. The `clara.clients` lookup runs as a SECURITY DEFINER owned by `clara_fn_owner`, which the owner policy `p_fixed_assets_owner`-style grants see across all firms, so an unknown uuid falls into the `v_firm is null` arm (CLR11 `client_not_found`) while another firm's real client falls THROUGH to the membership arm (CLR04 `obo_not_active`). Two different codes and two different reason tokens distinguish "this uuid is a client somewhere" from "this uuid is nothing" — the existence oracle the estate's CLR11 discipline (packages/db/tests/rig-helpers.mjs:64, "not-found-in-your-firm (NO existence oracle)") exists to close.
findings.evidence: `node --test <scratch>/adv639.test.mjs` on 55604/clara_639r printed `ORACLE: unknown-client -> CLR11/client_not_found   another-firm's-client -> CLR04/obo_not_active`. Tenant isolation itself is intact in the same run: firm-B human `get_fixed_asset` -> CLR11, firm-B `clara_agent_ro` direct `select ... from clara.fixed_assets` -> 0 rows, firm-B obo on a firm-A client -> CLR04, and no app role holds INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on `clara.fixed_assets`.
findings.fix: Either delete the claim from the comment, or make it true: resolve the obo's own active membership FIRST and raise CLR11 `client_not_found` whenever the caller's obo has no active membership in the client's firm, so an unknown uuid and a foreign client are indistinguishable. The caller is `clara_runtime` only, so the practical exposure is small — but the file should not assert a property it does not have.

findings.what: The cell's title claims four exclusions ("opening entries, reversal mirrors, disposals and scheduled depreciation runs birth NOTHING") but only two are behavioural. The reversal mirror (arm a) and the `fa_disposal` entry (arm b) drive real entries and count rows; `is_opening_balance` and `origin='scheduled_run'` are proven only by `body.includes(guard)` over `pg_proc.prosrc` (line 226). A string search cannot catch a guard that is present but ineffective — the exact failure mode brief-639.md:88 called out ("a guard admitting a K-family or scheduled-run entry is fixable only by a successor. Cells 3 and 4 are not optional") and TDD seam 4 asked for behaviourally ("K-family opening entries (belt door (e)) ... birth NOTHING. Red on any phantom row").
findings.evidence: Lines 220-227 are a `for (const guard of ["is_opening_balance", "reversal_of", "fa_disposal", "scheduled_run"])` loop over `prosrc`. The fresh-rig run (18/18 on 55604/clara_639r) printed no `exclusions(b)` degradation note, so arm b did assert — but no opening-balance entry and no `origin='scheduled_run'` entry is ever approved by this cell. I confirmed the guards ARE effective by reading 0041:2603 (arm 4's identical predicate) and 0041's arm 1, which raises CLR38 unless a depreciation proposal carries `origin='scheduled_run'` — so the residual risk today is low.
findings.fix: Add two behavioural arms: approve a K-family opening entry debiting the enrolled cost account through `_approve_opening_entry` / `_settle_opening_seed` and assert `assetCountOf(client)` is unmoved; run a real depreciation period (`runPeriod`, already imported from x41-fa-fixtures) on a complete neighbour and assert the `origin='scheduled_run'` charge entry births nothing. Keep the prosrc loop as a second belt, not as the only one.

findings.what: The door's headline claim is that "the authority is RE-READ LIVE rather than trusted from a snapshot" (0201:118-122), but the membership read at :761 takes no lock, and the door never takes `clara.firms ... for key share` first. 0195:1792-1797 records that exact pair as a MEASURED fix — `clara.set_member_role` (0157) takes `clara.firms ... for update` then UPDATEs the membership, so 0195's core takes the firm key-share first and then `firm_memberships ... for share` so a revocation queues behind the posting instead of deadlocking or slipping past. #639's door does neither, leaving a window in which a demotion commits between the role read and the register UPDATE. There is NO deadlock risk in the wrong direction (the door takes no membership lock at all, so no cycle with `set_member_role` exists — the only firms lock it takes is the implicit FK key-share from `_reserve_op`), which is why this is a note and not a blocker.
findings.evidence: 0201:761-763 is a bare `select m.role, m.status into v_role, v_status from clara.firm_memberships m where m.user_id = p_obo and m.firm_id = v_firm order by (m.status='active') desc, m.created_at desc limit 1` with no `for share`, and there is no `clara.firms` lock anywhere in the body (the only `perform pg_advisory_xact_lock` is in the shared core at :698, keyed on the client). Compare 0195:1792 `perform 1 from clara.firms f where f.id = p_firm for key share;` immediately followed by the same membership select with `for share`. My race probe confirms the door serialises correctly on the ASSET (CLR37 `fa_particulars_already_complete`), which is a different question from serialising against a demotion.
findings.fix: Mirror 0195:1792-1797 inside `complete_fixed_asset_particulars_for`: `perform 1 from clara.firms f where f.id = v_firm for key share;` before the membership select, and add `for share` to that select. Both are the weakest modes that queue behind `set_member_role`'s `for update`, and taking the firm row first keeps this door on the same lock order as the posting core, so no new 40P01 edge is introduced.
